prerequisites.reason: Understanding how individual neurons produce outputs is necessary to understand how feedforward networks compute layer-wise transformations.
Backpropagation computes gradients of the loss with respect to network parameters, so the notion of a loss function is required first.
Backpropagation relies on tracing derivatives through composed operations, which is captured by computational graphs.
To understand gradient flow through neural networks, one must understand the differentiable node functions used at each unit.
Backpropagation is used to provide gradients for parameter updates in gradient-based optimization, so understanding gradient descent is necessary context.
Backpropagation is typically defined over the layered structure and parameters of feedforward neural networks.
Feedforward networks are a foundational neural network architecture, and understanding them is necessary before broader neural network model families.
Activation functions are core building blocks used across neural network architectures.
Understanding the limitation of linear decision boundaries motivates why nonlinear activation functions are needed.
Gradient descent minimizes a loss function, so the optimization target must be understood first.
